personas.description: A likely-pathogenic variant (ACMG Class 4) — a real, verified discordance opposite to every other four-axis engine this session: classification is 'critical' (hasPathogenicVariant() includes 'likely-pathogenic') and follow-up escalates to 'critical-alert', but abnormalitySeverity is only 'moderate' (R-SEV-MODERATE-01), not 'major' — severity 'major' is reserved exclusively for the exact string 'pathogenic'. Every prior test-result engine this session paired 'critical' classification with 'major' severity; this one does not.

personas.name: carrier-status-positive-abnormal-recommended-not-urgent
personas.description: Positive carrier status for a recessive condition, with no top-level ACMG classification tier recorded for this carrier-screening report (a real, plausible documentation gap distinct from the diagnostic-variant reports above) and no secondary finding — classification abnormal, the same moderate-severity bucket as the secondary-finding persona above (R-SEV-MODERATE-02, shared rule ID), but follow-up is only 'recommended' (within 6 weeks, R-FU-RECOMMENDED-01) rather than 'urgent' — a real, verified divergence in Axis D between two findings that share the identical Axis B severity bucket. Note the deliberate contrast with the pathogenic-classified personas above: setting variantClassification to the literal string 'pathogenic' or 'likely-pathogenic' on a carrier report would instead trip hasPathogenicVariant() and sweep it into the critical/major path regardless of carrierStatusPositive, since classifyResult() checks pathogenicity before carrier status — the engine does not distinguish a variant causing disease in this patient from the same tier of variant carried in a single copy. Leaving the field unpopulated here (as this report genuinely does) is what keeps this persona on the carrier-status path, and correctly raises the missing-classification flag alongside it.

personas.name: variants-detected-no-classification-defaults-normal-missing-classification-flag
personas.description: A real, verified and arguably risky default: variants are described in free text but no structured ACMG classification was recorded and none of the interpretation booleans (pathogenicVariantFound, vusFound, carrierStatusPositive, secondaryFinding, noClinicallySignificantVariant) were set — classifyResult() has no catch-all for this state and falls all the way through to R-CLASS-NORMAL-02 ('No actionable variant or finding recorded'), classifying the report 'normal' even though a variant WAS described. The only safety net is F-MISSING-CLASSIFICATION-001, a flag rather than a classification change, confirmed to fire here (variantsDetected non-empty, variantClassification empty, noClinicallySignificantVariant false).
